title: Claimipedia candidates: source-first QFT and observable frontier
admission_policy: Admit only typed claims with explicit scope, evidence and dependency. Do not promote source-conditional Born values to Spin(2,3) predictions.

claims.claim: For the declared incidence and 3(B-L) currents in the Dirac-neutrino branch, the leading broken-phase fermion cut is a positive semidefinite real 2x2 spectral matrix with the explicit vector/axial threshold formula in the evidence document.
claims.scope: Born order; separated timelike momentum; dimensional regularization and MSbar; no Majorana mass; physical Dirac fermion thresholds

claims.claim: At Born order in the completed Dirac branch, the B-L/B-L and incidence/B-L longitudinal spectral cuts vanish, while the incidence/incidence longitudinal cut is nonnegative and mass suppressed.
claims.scope: same as FPQFT-C01; anomaly-free B-L; longitudinal convention declared in evidence
claims.falsifier: A nonzero separated-point longitudinal B-L cut in the same Dirac and anomaly-free branch after consistent Ward renormalization.

claims.claim: The massless one-generation transverse cuts reproduce Gram matrices [[231,9],[9,48]] and [[239,15],[15,48]] for the deduplicated and multiplicity-preserving incidence assignments respectively.
claims.scope: leading free ultraviolet cut in the declared current normalization

claims.claim: Coherent plus/minus source combinations isolate the signed mixed inclusive spectral density, and local polynomial source contacts cannot change its positive-energy discontinuity.
claims.scope: linearly coupled, calibrated weak sources with common kinematic normalization and an inclusive optical-theorem measurement
claims.first_missing_datum: an experimentally or microscopically realized pair of calibrated sources

claims.claim: The signed one-energy coherence is not invariant under the Ward-compatible finite shear J_lambda -> a J_lambda + b J_(B-L), so it cannot by itself select the incidence ray or constitute a source-free Spin(2,3) prediction.
claims.scope: positive-definite two-current response with unresolved affine source-frame freedom
claims.promotion_condition: derive the source frame from an action or operational coupling, or predict a common-congruence invariant of at least two response matrices

claims.claim: A complete interacting renormalization analysis must be performed in at least the seven-current unbroken-phase representative basis (or its six-dimensional external-source quotient), not solely in the incidence/B-L plane.
claims.scope: one generation with nu_R, canonical dimension-three Hermitian gauge-singlet vectors and the stated EOM/gradient quotient

claims.claim: The leading one-generation Yukawa source problem decomposes exactly into the D-orthogonal sum of ker(V)=span(Y,B,L) and the four-dimensional broken space D^{-1}im(V^T), with compressed positive block R=V D^{-1} V^T.
claims.scope: seven phase-current representatives, diagonal one-generation Yukawa channels, leading O(y^2) selection structure

claims.claim: For nonnegative channel weights the rank of the Yukawa mixing or divergence-response matrix equals the number of open independent Yukawa channels; all sixteen threshold masks obey this rule.
claims.scope: factorized matrix D^{-1}V^T W V or V^T W V with diagonal nonnegative W

claims.claim: Neither the deduplicated-incidence/B-L plane nor the multiplicity-incidence/B-L plane is invariant under any nonzero leading Yukawa weight assignment in the declared seven-current metric.
claims.scope: one generation, four Yukawa incidence rows, Gamma_Y=D^{-1}V^T W V; arbitrary real diagonal W
claims.promotion_condition: an additional physical projection or interaction derives a closed two-source subsystem not generated by Yukawa running alone

claims.claim: For an open dense set of positive Yukawa weights, the cyclic closure generated from incidence together with B-L has rank six and remains rank six after the hypercharge quotient: it fills the complete external global-source quotient.
claims.scope: same leading seven-current structure; generic means outside the zero set of the certified nonzero Krylov minor; the original incidence vector retains a second protected component while its iterates generate all four broken directions

claims.claim: The unevaluated part of the complete response separates into one-loop insertion poles, off-shell EOM/contact completion, two-loop nonlocal current-response masters, and broken-phase threshold matching; the block reduction alone does not determine their common coefficient or finite functions.
claims.scope: calculation inventory following the exact selection-rule reduction
claims.first_missing_datum: a gauge-complete rank-one up-Yukawa source calculation including EOM representatives and finite matching

claims.claim: With only the up Yukawa channel active, Gamma_u=w_u r_u v_u is rank one, obeys Gamma_u^2=(3w_u/2)Gamma_u, and the smallest invariant subsystem containing incidence and B-L has dimension three.
claims.scope: one-generation seven-current representative basis; up-channel selection structure; scalar channel weight left arbitrary

claims.claim: Allowing up, down, charged-lepton and neutrino Yukawa weights independently enlarges the smallest common invariant subsystem containing incidence and B-L through exact dimensions 3,4,5,6; the four-channel family fills the six-dimensional external-source quotient.
claims.scope: common invariance under the family of diagonal nonnegative channel weights, for either incidence normalization
claims.falsifier: A proper subspace containing the declared incidence and B-L vectors is invariant under all four independently weighted channel operators.

claims.claim: The up and down divergence channels cannot distinguish the two incidence normalizations; the charged-lepton channel is the first direct discriminator because their channel coordinates are (10,6,2,1) and (10,6,4,1).
claims.scope: channel-resolved leading Yukawa-divergence response

claims.claim: Every Yukawa-divergence channel annihilates B-L, so no collection of these four absorptive observables can determine the B-L shear of the incidence source.
claims.scope: Dirac-neutrino branch with V q_(B-L)=0; anomaly-sensitive and non-divergence observables excluded
claims.promotion_condition: add a separately calibrated vector-current or anomaly-sensitive observable that is not in the Yukawa-divergence family

claims.claim: The reduced charged-lepton/up divergence-rate ratio is 1/25 for deduplicated incidence and 4/25 for multiplicity-preserving incidence; the charged-lepton/down ratio is 1/9 versus 4/9.
claims.scope: channel-resolved leading Yukawa-divergence response after dividing the known channel spectral factors

claims.claim: The reduced two-channel ratio is invariant under a common source normalization and every shift in ker(V)=span(Y,B,L), including B-L shear, but not under an arbitrary change of the broken source direction.
claims.scope: projective broken-coordinate observable with nonzero calibrator channel
not_claimed: invariance under arbitrary GL transformations of the external-source space

claims.claim: Without an additional physical coupling that selects the incidence current, no Standard-Model S-matrix observable distinguishes the two incidence-source hypotheses; an ALP derivative coupling is a minimal realization, not a consequence of the Standard Model.
claims.scope: external-source incidence labels versus source-free Standard-Model observables
claims.promotion_condition: derive a coupling to the incidence current from the microscopic action or introduce and calibrate a mediator experimentally

claims.claim: In a fixed derivative-ALP embedding, a phase-space-reduced lepton/top partial-width ratio or a low-mass production-times-lifetime observable cancels the common ALP scale and can test the factor-two lepton-amplitude fork.
claims.scope: common matching prescription and flavor embedding; full running and thresholds required; no unprofiled independent gauge coefficients or extra invisible widths
claims.first_missing_datum: a matched two-hypothesis ALP scan for (-10,-6,-2) versus (-10,-6,-4) with gauge-operator and invisible-width nuisances profiled

claims.claim: For the dressed electron faces (H^dagger L,e^{c dagger}), the exact face-charge map F_e(x)=(x_L-x_H,-x_ec) pulls the face contrast (1,-1) back to the QFT charged-lepton divergence covector d_e=(0,0,0,1,1,0,-1).
claims.scope: one generation; declared seven-current basis; dressed-electron response realization

claims.claim: The operator representation on the dressed electron face pair decomposes into a common phase plus d_e(x)/2 times the traceless face contrast; 3(B-L) is purely common-phase while the two incidence candidates have contrasts 2 and 4.
claims.scope: infinitesimal internal source action on the dressed face doublet; response residues excluded

claims.claim: Anchoring the topology plane by the unoriented dressed-electron contrast reduces its residual SO(2) frame torsor to {+I,-I}; orienting the contrast removes the remaining sign.
claims.scope: the Kantor two-face metric/area plane after identification with the dressed-electron face module

claims.claim: The remaining physical bridge datum is a microscopic action or boundary functor mapping the abstract Furey/topology faces to the dressed electron pair while preserving dagger, Standard-Model action, Lorentz response typing and the Ward character; cyclic nonvanishing alone does not provide this functor.
claims.scope: promotion of the exact dressed-module intertwiner to an autonomous topology-to-QFT derivation
claims.first_missing_datum: an action-derived topology-to-dressed-electron response functor Phi_phys

claims.claim: Within the one-generation one-Higgs Standard Model field content, L e^c H^dagger is the unique local renormalizable gauge- and Lorentz-invariant one-scalar/two-Weyl operator containing e^c, and its infinitesimal source character is d_e.
claims.scope: engineering-dimension-four operators with the declared Standard-Model fields; higher-dimensional and extended-scalar operators excluded

claims.claim: A local Standard-Model action with background phase sources generates rho_e=diag(x_L-x_H,-x_ec) and the Ward term proportional to y_e d_e(x), with anomaly, EOM and contact completion as required.
claims.scope: classical local Ward identity and its consistently renormalized operator form; no claim that y_e or finite response residues are derived

claims.claim: Furey TRO and linking-algebra incidence data do not imply the cyclic block-trace interaction rule: actions with y_e=0 and arbitrary complex y_e have identical representation, arrow and block-product data.
claims.scope: derivation of action coefficients or interaction presence from algebraic incidence alone
claims.promotion_condition: supply an independently derived action functional, Dirac/Higgs operator or cyclic cocycle assigning a nonzero coefficient to the electron cycle

claims.claim: The electron Ward character fixes neither the Yukawa coefficient nor a scalar positive response normalization; the unbroken dressed faces have unequal dimensions and opposite Weyl typing, so a broken-phase scale and Lorentz/spectral projection are additional data.
claims.scope: promotion from the exact source-character intertwiner to a normalized H2(R) response kernel
claims.first_missing_datum: a Lorentz-compatible projection of the Dirac two-point kernel with a fixed spectral normalization

claims.claim: For a canonically normalized free on-shell electron of helicity h, the trace-normalized chiral pole residue [[E-hk,m],[m,E+hk]]/(2E) is a positive rank-one projector in H2(R); its rest-frame value is one half times the all-ones matrix.
claims.scope: one generation, real positive mass convention, positive-energy pole, declared helicity convention

claims.claim: The separated-point chiral Kallen-Lehmann block is positive when rho_L and rho_R are nonnegative and s rho_L rho_R is at least |rho_m|^2; it lies in H2(R) only when the off-diagonal spectral phase admits one common real convention.
claims.scope: rest-frame spin-reduced two-face spectral measure; momentum-dependent irreducible phases require H2(C)

claims.claim: Local quadratic source contacts have no positive-energy spectral measure or isolated pole residue, while EOM semilocal terms, anomaly channels and composite-operator renormalization must be handled separately from the positive electron spectral block.
claims.scope: spectral definition from separated-point Wightman functions; does not discard Ward contacts from the full time-ordered identity

claims.claim: The normalized positive electron pole is canonical after pole isolation and rest-frame spin averaging, but its identification with the Furey faces and the interacting relative overlap z_L/z_R are conditional action and renormalization data not fixed by d_e.
claims.scope: renormalized dressed pair ((sqrt(2)/v) H^dagger L, e^{c dagger})
claims.first_missing_datum: a gauge-consistent renormalization or measurement of the dressed composite pole-overlap ratio z_L/z_R

claims.claim: The helicity-resolved normalized pole obeys A_h^2+C_h^2=1 with chirality asymmetry A_h=h k/E and real chiral coherence C_h=m/E; equivalently the wrong-chirality probability is (1-k/E)/2.
claims.scope: free or isolated canonically normalized electron pole measured with a chirality-sensitive polarization analyzer
not_claimed: a derivation of the physical incidence ray

claims.claim: Canonical tree fields, v-normalization of H^dagger L and a real-positive electron mass give z_L/z_R=1 at the rest-frame one-electron pole.
claims.scope: free broken-phase Dirac electron; infrared-regulated sharp-pole convention

claims.claim: A finite relative operator renormalization O_L->a O_L, O_R->b O_R changes z_L/z_R by a/b and changes the normalized pole ray, while inverse-renormalizing the sources leaves all complete amplitudes invariant.
claims.scope: nonzero finite diagonal changes of the dressed-electron interpolating-operator basis
claims.falsifier: a physical symmetry or source normalization that forbids relative finite rescaling of the two interpolators

claims.claim: LSZ, the interacting Dirac/EOM relation, CP, CPT and the renormalized Yukawa Ward identity do not fix the magnitude of z_L/z_R: they fix state normalization, operator products, phases or conjugate-channel relations, while a positive relative finite rescaling remains.
claims.scope: Standard Model without an additional exact left-right exchange symmetry; complete Ward/EOM/contact basis retained

claims.claim: Only calibrated combinations such as g_L z_L and g_R z_R are observable; the overlap ratio alone requires an operator-renormalization condition or independently calibrated source ratio.
claims.scope: dressed-electron pole or infrared-regulated pole-like response
claims.first_missing_datum: an EOM/on-shell composite renormalization condition or a calibrated two-source measurement
not_claimed: an exact nonperturbative isolated electron pole in massless QED

claims.claim: The four coherent intensity settings L, R, L+R and L+iR have rank four on H2(C) and reconstruct the calibrated two-face response, hence a rank-one amplitude pair up to common phase; on a verified real slice the first three settings have rank three and suffice.
claims.scope: phase-stable calibrated sources with a common interfering final-state sum

claims.claim: Pure left and right rates cannot determine a relative sign; a coherent real superposition is required for the sign and a quadrature-shifted superposition is required for a general complex phase.
claims.scope: intensity-only tomography of two calibrated amplitude components

claims.claim: For the two fixed positive incidence hypotheses, one calibrated charged-lepton/top magnitude ratio distinguishes the rays by a factor four at bare rate level; this restricted test is not complete two-face tomography and does not determine sign.
claims.scope: hypothesis set restricted to (10,6,2,1) and (10,6,4,1) with common source calibration

claims.claim: In the fixed generation-universal ALPaca benchmark, deduplicated and multiplicity-preserving incidence have kaon production rates equal within 10^-4 but proper-lifetime ratios 2.773 at 100 MeV and 2.758 at 300 MeV.
claims.scope: ALPaca 1.2.0; 10 TeV matching; f_a=10^6 GeV; cG=cW=cB=0; no right-handed neutrino

claims.claim: Using the published NA62 300 MeV prompt curve and lifetime acceptance approximation, the fixed deduplicated and multiplicity benchmarks cross at f_a approximately 1.804e6 and 2.319e6 GeV respectively, but upper-limit curves with free f_a do not identify either ray.
claims.scope: curve-level recast rather than collaboration likelihood; fixed matching and nuisance assumptions

claims.claim: A robust low-mass ALP incidence test with unknown width composition minimally requires kaon production, proper lifetime and leptonic branching fraction; production-times-lifetime alone suffices only after assuming a lepton-dominated total width and restricted UV nuisances.
claims.scope: top-seeded rare-kaon production used as calibrator for a charged-lepton partial width
claims.first_missing_datum: a signal-level joint likelihood for production, lifetime and visible branching fractions with gauge, flavor and invisible-width nuisances profiled

claims.claim: The complete supplied one-family triplet-channel set with nonzero QQ, u^c e^c and d^c nu^c channels produces a non-scalar positive spectral Gram kernel, but at h=f and equal channel weights neither q_QQ=(1,1,1) nor the algebraic safe vector (-2,1,1) is an eigenvector.
claims.scope: triplet basis (10, 126bar_5, 126bar_50), supplied Clebsch rows, real one-family Yukawas and positive Euclidean channel weights

claims.claim: Two allowed action points with identical nonzero Clebsch support, (h,f)=(1,1) and (2,1), yield noncommuting triplet-copy Gram kernels; therefore representation content and support alone do not define a common canonical eigendirection on W.
claims.scope: canonical orientation claimed uniformly over the allowed 10- and 126-Yukawa parameter family
claims.falsifier: an additional exact symmetry or UV matching condition that fixes the Yukawa ratio and all threshold weights

claims.claim: A QQ-only rank-one self-energy selects q_QQ only after the QQ Clebsch row and equal Yukawa-dressed coefficients are supplied; unequal allowed coefficients rotate the selected line, so this construction realizes rather than derives the QQ orientation.
claims.scope: rank-one truncations of the exceptional triplet response

claims.claim: A symmetry-allowed Hermitian finite mass or wave-function counterterm can rotate the q_QQ eigendirection, and identical finite-Dirac support can yield noncommuting D_F^dagger D_F operators; neither an off-shell loop eigenvector nor support alone is a scheme-independent selector.
claims.scope: three copies with identical unbroken gauge quantum numbers and no additional character forbidding copy mixing
not_claimed: that pole locations or complete S-matrix elements of a fully specified renormalized model are scheme dependent

claims.claim: Fixing the exceptional triplet action and its non-scalar K_W does not choose between lambda_D and lambda_M: both source rays remain compatible because the audited action contains no typed map from the seven-current source space to triplet-copy space.
claims.scope: current corpus without an independently derived cross-carrier intertwiner
claims.first_missing_datum: a symmetry-protected typed map Y_F from the seven-current source carrier to W whose coefficients are derived independently of q_QQ
